item.description: In the 1840s, Shakespeare's birthplace in Stratford-upon-Avon faced the threat of sale, as American showman P.T. Barnum aimed to move the historic home to New York. A dedicated committee formed, rallying public donations and support from notable figures like Prince Albert to save the site. Their efforts culminated in the successful acquisition of the house at auction in 1847, ensuring the preservation of this cherished cultural landmark. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: ‘They do look majestic’: tears and pride as first white storks set free in Cornwall
item.description: Twenty-one birds released on Bodmin Moor where it is hoped they will one day return to produce their own young They took a little coaxing at first – after all, they had got used to a safe, comfortable aviary tucked away in woodland on the edge of Bodmin Moor. But after a few minutes, the birds stepped out into freedom and the bolder ones were soon soaring into the blue, the first white storks to be released into the wilds of Cornwall. Yan Swiderski, the founder of the Cornwall Stork Project , had tears in his eyes. “I do feel a bit emotional,” he said. He sounded a little like a proud father… Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Egyptian archaeologists uncover 3 tombs, 5 mummies, and Roman remains
item.description: An Egyptian archaeological mission has uncovered three tombs at the Sheikh Sobi site. These burials include mummies and sarcophagi from the Late and Roman periods. One tomb contained five mummies, dating to the Late Period. The other two tombs are believed to be from the Roman period. These discoveries offer insights into the Bahariya Oasis's ancient communities. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Morocco is testing a 'sponge' pavement that stays 16°F cooler by itself, aims at replacing black asphalt
item.description: Morocco is pioneering a novel sponge pavement designed to enhance water management and mitigate heat effects. Unlike conventional black asphalt, this innovative surface enables water to seep through, promoting natural cooling through evaporation when moisture exists. This initiative aims to bolster urban climate resilience and elevate the comfort of residents, with pilot projects underway in Marrakech and Agadir as part of a larger sustainable city initiative. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
